title: TS-70 The second computer start after a host exit waited about 55 s before the starter ran
description: From the live git-task rehearsal (2026-10-07): the first start ran the ComputerStarter 2 to 6 s after the post (post to host ready about 23 s with the slim image). The second start, after the first host exited by itself, invoked the starter about 55 s after the post (post to host ready about 80 s); after the starter ran, task startup was normal (created, started in 15 s, ready 8 s later). The ComputerStarter and TurnProbe logs show only START, END and REPORT lines, no errors. Find what gates the second start after a host exit (candidates: the host start lease or claim window in domain/computer-start.ts, the TS-58 reconciliation path, the probe interval, the start job dedupe window, SQS delivery). Needs the structured logging of TS-55 to see it; add the log lines first or alongside. A scenario that proves a start requested after a host exit is dispatched immediately. Mutation checks.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Root cause: a cleanly exited host leaves its worker record registered, so for up to 30 s assignTurn counted it healthy and a parked turn published no start job. Fixed in PR 475 (assignTurn treats a stopped computer as having no live host). Scenarios: clean exit queues a start at once; running host not asked to start; booting host started once. Mutation-checked. Known caveat: a boot longer than the 60 s start lease with a turn arriving after it expires claims a second generation. The registry also keeps one worker id (computer-host) for every host, which hid the first host's heartbeat.

right_now_summary: A stopped host stayed registered as healthy, delaying the next computer start by up to 30 seconds.
